changelog:
Internet-class enforcement: discovery now accepts only DNS class IN records (while preserving mDNS cache-flush and question unicast-response bits), preventing unrelated class data from being interpreted as Hue service endpoints.
Regression coverage: discovery tests reject non-Internet question and resource-record classes and retain compatibility with the mDNS cache-flush bit.
Backward-only pointers: discovery now rejects forward DNS compression pointers, which are invalid on the wire and could otherwise manufacture service/host associations from later records.
Regression coverage: discovery tests verify forward-pointer responses fail closed without returning a bridge address.
RDATA bounds: PTR and SRV discovery names are now parsed only within each DNS record's declared RDATA, rejecting malformed packets that would otherwise consume bytes from a following record.
Name safety: compressed-name pointers are bounds checked and decoded names are capped at the DNS wire-format maximum.
Regression coverage: discovery tests verify truncated SRV records fail closed without returning a bridge address.
Scoped link-local transport: mDNS-discovered IPv6 link-local bridge addresses now preserve their interface scope when converted into HTTPS request URIs, so multi-interface hosts can connect to the selected bridge instead of silently dropping the scope.
Certificate-pin identity parity: URI-encoded IPv6 zone identifiers are normalized back to the persisted bridge spelling before certificate-pin lookup.
Regression coverage: Hue client tests verify both HTTP-safe scoped URI construction and scoped IPv6 certificate-pin identity normalization.
Whitespace edge-case closure: the 4,096-character channel-profile limit is now checked before blank-value handling, so oversized whitespace-only input is bounded consistently with every other supplied value.
Regression coverage: parser tests cover oversized valid-token and whitespace-only values while preserving blank-field inheritance below the limit.
Parser allocation guard: administrator-supplied global, per-user, and device-route channel profiles now reject text longer than 4,096 characters before tokenization, keeping malformed configuration input bounded without changing valid channel IDs or delimiter behavior.
UI contract parity: channel-profile editors expose the same 4,096-character limit, and regression coverage verifies oversized input is rejected before parsing.
Resolver result validation: durable cleanup recovery now re-checks injected or host-provided bridge resolver results against the private/link-local/unique-local boundary before treating an alias as the same physical bridge.
Regression coverage: scheduler recovery tests reject non-local resolver results without contacting a bridge.
Administrator delete lifecycle safety: single user-mapping deletes now bind confirmation and DELETE callbacks to the active configuration page, cancel on page teardown, prevent duplicate submissions, and suppress stale reloads/resets.
Durable cleanup alias recovery: scheduled cleanup journals now reconcile IP/.local bridge aliases through vetted local addresses or matching certificate pins, while mismatched/ambiguous targets remain fail-closed.
Regression coverage: lifecycle and scheduler tests cover stale mapping-delete confirmation/completion, alias recovery, and unrelated-target rejection.
Gitleaks false-positive boundary: the default Gitleaks rules remain active while only public example fixtures in the reviewed Semgrep snapshot directory are allowlisted, with a contract test preventing broader exclusions.
Reviewed Semgrep snapshots: blocking self-hosted and PR scans now use SHA-256-verified local registry snapshots, preventing mutable aliases or CDN responses from changing policy mid-run.
Install-failure isolation: sub-scans only run after a successful hash-locked Semgrep install, preventing stale runner-temp files from being mistaken for current scan inputs.
Regression coverage: the Semgrep lock validator verifies snapshot paths, file digests, workflow parity, and safe scan gating.
Certificate trust alias safety: bridge certificate pins now resolve IP and .local aliases against a single vetted local address, fail closed on conflicting fingerprints, and keep registration, credential-free probes, transport TLS validation, playback arbitration, and pin management aligned.
Regression coverage: API and certificate-validation tests cover alias equivalence, conflict rejection, alias cleanup, unknown-target protection, and credential-free probe behavior.
User-mapping save lifecycle safety: mapping saves are tracked against the active configuration page, duplicate submissions are bounded, teardown and edit cancellation abort in-flight writes, and stale callbacks cannot alert, reload mappings, or reset a newer draft.
Regression coverage: configuration contracts cover complete mapping payloads, duplicate-submit protection, pagehide cancellation, stale callback suppression, success reloads, and button-state restoration.
Semgrep snapshot integrity: refresh the reviewed SHA-256 pin for the current default ruleset snapshot after the registry rotated; blocking scans continue to fail closed on any unreviewed change.
Scheduled-run identity safety: manual Run Now cancellation remains bound to the cue ID that started the run, even if the administrator changes the selection; stale run callbacks cannot mutate a reused page.
Preview/capture lifecycle safety: page teardown cancels in-flight preview, capture, and cancellation requests; stale callbacks cannot hide loading UI or overwrite an active page.
Recurrence search hardening: cached normalized exclusion dates avoid reparsing exclusions for every candidate, and a maximum DateTime boundary guard prevents overflow with stale skip markers.
Selector and accessibility hardening: persisted entertainment-area IDs are matched without selector interpolation, and diagnostics/mapping tables expose captions and column scopes.
Regression coverage: configuration contracts cover cancellation identity, page lifecycle races, unsafe area IDs, and scheduler boundary conditions.

Regression coverage: scheduler tests cover long recurrence intervals and the administrator configuration contract covers stale certificate trust prompts.

Regression coverage: serializer-backed scheduler tests cover preclaim failure, deferred retry, reconstructed restart suppression, and the administrator color-preset lifecycle contract.

Adds mDNS DNS-class validation so unrelated class data cannot be interpreted as a Hue endpoint, while preserving cache-flush and unicast-response flag compatibility, with regression coverage. Adds backward-only DNS compression-pointer validation so malformed mDNS responses cannot manufacture service/host associations from later records, with regression coverage. Adds mDNS parser RDATA bounds and compressed-name safety so malformed local discovery responses fail closed, with regression coverage for truncated SRV records. Preserves IPv6 link-local interface scopes in bridge HTTPS transport and certificate-pin identity lookup, with regression coverage for multi-interface discovery. Tightens the channel-profile length guard to reject oversized whitespace-only values before blank handling while preserving ordinary blank-field inheritance, with regression coverage. Adds a bounded channel-profile parser and matching administrator input limits so malformed channel text cannot trigger unbounded tokenization, with regression coverage and unchanged valid delimiter behavior. Adds resolver-result boundary validation so durable cleanup recovery cannot treat a public address as a vetted bridge alias, with regression coverage for fail-closed rejection. Adds administrator mapping-delete lifecycle guards and durable scheduled-cleanup recovery across IP/.local bridge aliases, with fail-closed target validation and regression coverage. Refreshes the reviewed Semgrep default-ruleset SHA-256 pin after registry rotation while retaining fail-closed blocking scans. Adds null-safe playback-event filtering and bounded FFmpeg version, stderr, and PCM probes that terminate oversized output fail-closed. Adds event-scoped security-scan concurrency so scheduled scans cannot cancel trusted main-push gates. Adds source-bound release provenance: schema-version-2 manifests now bind the tested package and all release assets to the exact 40-character source commit, with helper parity and isolated release-runner verification. Adds the Matrix scene effect: deterministic green/cyan cascading data-rain trails with smooth envelopes and independent channel phases across previews, saved scenes, playlists, scheduled cues, and credential-free portability. Adds a restart-safe scheduled cleanup journal that persists bounded credential-free snapshots before activation, retries bridge deactivation and light restoration after restart, and exposes sanitized pending-cleanup telemetry. Adds immediate post-commit shutdown for disabled global and per-user Hue Sync policies, selective concurrent-session reconciliation, safe light restoration, and fail-closed duplicate-mapping handling. Adds shutdown-durable manual schedule cancellation with service-owned stop state, cancellation outside locks, and awaited restorative cleanup. Adds cancellation-safe automatic occurrence retention for failed transport results across direct scenes and fallback playlists. Adds lifecycle-safe saved-scene duplication with request tracking, teardown cancellation, stale-response suppression, and duplicate-submit protection. Adds scheduler and administrator lifecycle regression coverage. Adds restart-durable at-most-once claims for automatic one-time cues, persisting disablement before bridge or deferred-expiry consumption and failing closed on claim persistence errors. Adds lifecycle-safe saved color-preset saves with teardown cancellation, duplicate-submit protection, and stale-response suppression. Adds retryable one-time schedule completion persistence that keeps successful cues disabled without replaying bridge activity. Adds CODEOWNERS coverage for CI, dependency, and security policy files while preserving the trusted owner-only direct-main release bypass. Adds deferred scheduler durability: expired deferred one-time cues clear stale Skip Next markers with completed state, and failed deferred-state writes retry from the authoritative runtime snapshot without duplicate bridge activity or replay. Adds deferred one-time Skip Next cancellation that safely consumes persisted waits, disables completed cues, and records skipped/deferred history through single and bulk administrator APIs. Adds history-only scheduler clearing that preserves pending deferred cues and retries; host-shutdown sync-loop cancellation now defers bridge restoration until the predecessor exits and retries deactivation with a fresh cleanup token. Semgrep gates now split production/configuration and repository-script scans, block fixpoint timeouts, and verify reviewed SHA-256-pinned rule snapshots. Matching-target scheduler playback conflicts now use the evaluated configuration snapshot's certificate identity, with regression coverage for cancellation/retry and snapshot-consistent arbitration. The executable Dependabot contract requires this policy in every tracked NuGet project block.
